[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Lucky Permutation** [CF 1768D · Lucky Permutation](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1768/D){rating="1800"}

A permutation with exactly one inversion is the identity with one adjacent pair $(k, k+1)$ swapped. Sorting costs $n - c$ swaps ($c$ = number of cycles). If some $k$ and $k + 1$ lie on the same cycle, stop one swap early and leave them as a 2-cycle: $n - c - 1$. Otherwise one extra swap is unavoidable: $n - c + 1$.

[Solved in full in @sec-idx-p3-lucky.]{.card-link}
